QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.claim: Transgressors exceed human nature’s balance toward animal or predatory ranks and prefer sensory pleasure to real life, so hell becomes their home.
QASHANI:79:34-41/r4.anchor: تعدى طور الفطرة الإنسانية وجاوز حد العدالة والشريعة إلى الرتبة البهيمية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r4.claim: The transgressor is one who disbelieves and prefers worldly life to the hereafter; Hell is his home.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r4.anchor: {فأما من طغى} في كفره. {وآثر الحياة الدنيا} على الآخرة. {فإن الجحيم هي المأوى وأما من خاف مقام ربه

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r2.claim: He preferred worldly life, immersing himself in it without preparing for the afterlife through worship and disciplining the soul.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:37-40/r2.anchor: { وءاثر الحيوة الدنيا } فانهمك فيها ولم يستعد للآخرة بالعبادة وتهذيب النفس

BINTSHATI:v1p155/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p155/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p155/r4.claim: Athara means a remaining trace or legacy, and here preferring worldly life evokes what one chooses to retain or leave behind.
BINTSHATI:v1p155/r4.anchor: الأثر، لغة: بقية الشيء، ومنه الخبر المأثور الباقي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r1.claim: The transgressor prefers immediate worldly life over the unseen afterlife, behaves like an animal limited to present things, and neglects worship and self-discipline.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r1.anchor: بأن جعل أثر العاجلة الدنية لحضورها عنده أعظم من أثر الآخرة العليا لغيابها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r8.claim: The rhetorical arrangement uses transgression to imply the opposite of restraint and restraint to imply rejection of worldly preference.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p320/r8.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : أتى بطغى دليلا على ضده ثانيا , وبالنهي عن الهوى ثانيا دلالة على إيثار الدنيا أولا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r1.claim: Leaders prefer worldly life because, despite recognizing the Messenger's truth, they resent following another and losing their authority.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p92/r1.anchor: فإن سادتهم ومسيريهم يعلمون أن ما يدعوهم إليه الرسول هو الحق ولكنهم يكرهون متابعته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r1.claim: طغى means crossing proper human limits through disbelief and preferring worldly life because of denying the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r1.anchor: طغى معناه: تجاوز الحدود التي ينبغي للإنسان أن يقف عندها بأن كفر وآثر الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r4.claim: The rebel is one who defies God and prefers worldly life over religion and the Hereafter; Hell is his destination, with food from zaqqum and drink of boiling water.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r4.anchor: أي: تمرد وعتا، {وآثر الحياة الدنيا} أي: قدمها على أمر دينه وأخراه،

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r7.claim: Choosing worldly life over the Hereafter is blameworthy, whereas choosing the Hereafter is praiseworthy.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r7.anchor: فمن آثر الدنيا على الآخرة فهو مذموم، ومن آثر الآخرة فهو ممدوح

JISHUMI:v10p7277/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r2.claim: Preferring worldly life and working for it while heedless of the Hereafter is blameworthy.
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r2.anchor: أن من آثر الدنيا وعمل لها غافلا عن الآخرة فقد ارتكب أمرا قبيحا

RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.claim: After describing Resurrection generally, God divides those morally responsible into wretched and blessed, beginning with the wretched.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47/r4.anchor: قسم المكلفين قسمين : الأشقياء والسعداء ، فذكر حال الأشقياء

TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.claim: The passage divides people into two exemplary classes, introducing Hell's people first because the address targets polytheists; transgression and preferring worldly life define the former, fear and restraint the latter.
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r6.anchor: وقدم صفة أهل الجحيم لأن وجه الكلام إلى المشركين

TABATABAI:79:38-41/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r1.claim: Transgression entails rejecting the afterlife, preferring worldly life, and following the self's desires; the opposite is fear that restrains attachment to the world and forbids following desire.
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r1.anchor: كان لما يقابل الطغيان من الوصف وهو الخوف ما يقابل الإيثار واتباع هوى النفس

TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.claim: The two classes are unbelieving wrongdoers and faithful, pious people; the fate of the weak and those mixing good and bad deeds is left to God, who may forgive or accept intercession.
TABATABAI:79:38-41/r3.anchor: وهناك غير الطائفتين طوائف أخر من المستضعفين والذين اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.claim: These brief verses summarize negative and positive attitudes that prepare either immense loss or salvation in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r1.anchor: Bu birkaç kısa âyette âhiretteki büyük kaybı veya büyük kurtuluşu hazırlayan olumsuz ve olumlu tutumların çok veciz bir özeti yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r2.claim: Ṭughyān is contrasted with hilm in al-Tur 52:33 and describes the impulsive, unthinking, stubborn, unbelieving attitude of pre-Islamic people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r2.anchor: “Azgınlık” diye çevirdiğimiz “tuğyân” kavramı Tûr sûresinde (52/33) “akıllı ve ağırbaşlı düşünüp davranma” mânasındaki “hilm”in karşıtı olarak kullanılır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r3.claim: Such people usually live for the immediate moment and do not look beyond the transient world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:37/r3.anchor: Böyleleri genellikle anlık yaşadıkları için fâni dünyanın ötesine bakmazlar

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r7.claim: Preferring worldly life reflects corruption of the practical faculty; paired with transgression, it marks maximal corruption and the unbeliever whose punishment is everlasting.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r7.anchor: وقوله : { وءاثر الحيواة الدنيا } إشارة إلى فساد حال القوة العملية

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r8.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r8.claim: Rāzī cites the Prophetic saying that love of the world is the root of every sin to support this diagnosis of practical corruption.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r8.anchor: لما روي عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قال : ( حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة )

STUDYQURAN:79:37/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī reads preferring worldly life as corruption in action.
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r2.anchor: Prefers the life of this world is then taken to indicate corruption in actions

STUDYQURAN:79:37/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r3.claim: The commentary cites a hadith saying love of the world is the source of all error.
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r3.anchor: The love of the world is the source of all error

STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.claim: Together, intellectual and practical corruption represent the greatest corruption and merit eternal punishment; Hell is the refuge for those reaching this level.
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r4.anchor: The two together are thus taken to indicate the greatest degree of corruption, the punishment for which is eternal

STUDYQURAN:79:37/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r6.claim: Other verses condemn preferring worldly life: it is delusive enjoyment, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring.
STUDYQURAN:79:37/r6.anchor: Many verses condemn those who prefer the life of this world over the life of the Hereafter

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r1.claim: The person who transgresses and prefers worldly life is a disbeliever.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {فأما من طغى (37) وآثر الحياة الدنيا} يعني الكافر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r2.speaker: مقاتل، الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r2.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say the verses were revealed about al-Nadr and his father al-Harith.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p200/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل (¬5)، والكلبي (¬6): نزلت في النضر وأبيه الحرث

BURHAN:v4p37/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p37/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p37/r11.claim: A context that calls for a pronoun may instead use an explicit noun; the author refers readers to his earlier discussion under emphasis.
BURHAN:v4p37/r11.anchor: ومنها الاسم الظاهر بأن يكون المقام يقتضي الإضمار فيعدل عنه إلى الظاهر وقد سبق الكلام عليه في أبواب التأكيد

BURHAN:v4p37/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p37/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p37/r12.claim: A pronoun normally refers to the nearest preceding noun, but after a construct it refers to the head noun, the topic, rather than its genitive complement.
BURHAN:v4p37/r12.anchor: الأصل في الضمير عوده إلى أقرب مذكور ولنا أصل آخر وهو أنه إذا جاء مضاف ومضاف إليه وذكر بعدهما ضمير عاد إلى المضاف

SULAMI:v2p371#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r1.claim: Transgression means denying God’s rights and rejecting His blessings, while preferring worldly life by pursuing desires and passions.
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r1.anchor: قال سهل : جحد حقوق الله وكفر نعمه وآثر الحياة الدنيا اتباعا في طلب الشهوات

SULAMI:v2p371#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r3.claim: Abu ʿUthman defines transgression as turning away from the afterlife and turning toward worldly life.
SULAMI:v2p371#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان : الطغيان الإعراض عن الآخرة والإقبال على الدنيا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r1.claim: Jurjānī frames the book’s aim as mapping how meanings converge or diverge, classifying them, and tracing their differing relations to reason and to borrowed status.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r1.anchor: غرضي في هذا الكلام الذي أبتدأته والأساس الذي وضعته أن أتوصل إلى بيان أمر المعاني كيف تتفق وتختلف ومن أين تجتمع وتفترق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r2.claim: Some speech has intrinsic worth like gold despite changing forms; other speech depends on crafted form, and loses its value when that form is stripped away.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r2.anchor: ما هو كما هو شريف في جوهرة كالذهب الأبريز الذي تختلف عليه الصور وتتعاقب عليه الصناعات وجل المعول في شرفه على ذاته

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r3.claim: Simile, representation, and metaphor are the first tools to study because most, perhaps all, beauties of speech branch from them.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p19/r3.anchor: على التشبيه والتمثيل والاستعارة فإن هذه أصول كثيرة كان جل محاسن الكلام إن لم نقل كلها متفرعة عنها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r1.claim: Grammar is indispensable for understanding the Qurʾān: parsing unlocks meanings and purposes and supplies the standard for judging soundness and merit; neglecting it is a loss despite the available gain.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r1.anchor: الألفاظ مغلقة على معانيها حتى يكون الإعراب هو الذي يفتحها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r2.claim: The author concedes that contrived morphology drills, such as weighing rare words or testing hypothetical names, need not be studied and are not his concern.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r2.anchor: أما هذا الجنس فلسنا نعيبكم إن لم تنظروا فيه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r3.claim: Serious grammatical inquiry asks about the purposes and wisdom of linguistic conventions and the regular measures that govern them.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r3.anchor: وتجاوزوه إلى الكلام على أغراض واضع اللغة ، وعلى وجه الحكمة في الأوضاع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r4.claim: The author points to the changes affecting weak wāw, yāʾ, and alif through substitution, deletion, and vowellessness as proper subjects of inquiry.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r5.claim: The dual and sound plural inflect differently from the singular, and their accusative follows the genitive.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r5.anchor: لم كان إعرابهما على خلاف إعراب الواحد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r6.claim: The nūn substitutes for both vowel and tanwīn in one case and for the vowel alone in another.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r6.anchor: وفي النون أنه عوض عن الحركة والتنوين في حال

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p42/r7.claim: The author treats the causes of diptote declension as reasoned secondary causes: two causes or a repeated cause make a noun secondary in two respects, like the verb relative to the noun.

TUSTARI:79:37-38/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r2.claim: Preferring worldly life means pursuing pleasures and following one's desires.
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r2.anchor: آثر الحياة الدنيا اتباعا في طلب الشهوات ومتابعة المراد

TUSTARI:79:37-38/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r3.claim: Everyone is ignorant except the one who prefers God over self, spirit, this world, and the afterlife.
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r3.anchor: ما طلعت شمس ولا غربت على أحد إلا وهو جاهل، إلا من يؤثر الله تعالى على نفسه وروحه ودنياه وآخرته

TUSTARI:79:37-38/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r4.claim: A sign of disaffection from worldly life is that calamities become light, even the loss of one's child or self.
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r4.anchor: قيل: ما علامة بغض الدنيا؟ قال: أن تهون عليه المصائب، حتى نفسه وولده

TUSTARI:79:37-38/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r5.speaker: مسلم بن يسار
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r5.claim: When his son died, Muslim b. Yasar said grief for his son had distracted him from grieving over him, and asked God to make the reward he received through the loss belong to his son.
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r5.anchor: كما قال مسلم بن يسار حين مات ولده: يا بني، شغلني الحزن لك عن الحزن عليك

TUSTARI:79:37-38/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r6.claim: A second sign is that even the pleasures of worldly life, including one's own life, become of little weight.
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r6.anchor: والثاني يهون عليه نعيم الدنيا ولو روحه

TUSTARI:79:37-38/r7.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r7.speaker: author
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r7.claim: A third sign is that nothing is nearer to the person than God.
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r7.anchor: والثالث لا يكون شيء أقرب إليه من الله عز وجل

TUSTARI:79:37-38/r8.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r8.speaker: عامر بن عبد القيس
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r8.claim: Amir ibn Abd al-Qays said that whenever he looked at anything, he saw God nearer to it than himself.
TUSTARI:79:37-38/r8.anchor: كقول عامر بن عبد القيس: ما نظرت إلى شيء إلا رأيت الله أقرب إليه مني

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r1.claim: The figure sniffs, follows the scent with its muzzle as with a rock-breaking axe, and thereby investigates.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r1.anchor: يريد: أنه يشتمم ثم يتبع الرائحة بخطم كأنه الفأس التي يكسر بها الصخر، فجعل تشممه استخبارا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r2.claim: Arabic metaphorically says a wall 'said' and leaned, or that an animal 'said'; it does not ordinarily call these actions speaking, which requires vocal utterance.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r2.anchor: فيقال: قال الحائط فمال، وقل برأسك إلي، أي أمله، وقالت الناقة، وقال البعير. ولا يقال في مثل هذا المعنى: تكلم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r3.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r3.claim: The anonymous poem lets silent graves and fading tongues admonish and speak because their signs convey a lesson.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر : وعظتك أجداث صمت ... ونعتك ألسنة خفت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r4.speaker: الكميت
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r4.claim: Al-Kumayt says the earth reported a man's deeds, meaning his canals, trees, and other traces made his work visible.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r4.anchor: وقال الكميت يمدح رجلا : أخبرت عن فعاله الأرض واستن

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r5.speaker: عوف بن الخرع
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r5.claim: The ruined house cannot answer literally; its visible state indicates its history like a whisper.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r5.anchor: وقال عوف بن الخرع يذكر الدار : وقفت بها ما تبين الكلام ... لسائلها القول إلا سرارا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r6.claim: The sages' saying that every silent thing speaks means that workmanship points to its maker and director.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r6.anchor: ولهذا قالت الحكماء: كل صامت ناطق. يريدون أن أثر الصنعة فيه يدل على محدثه ومدبره

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r8.claim: Metaphorical actions do not take an emphatic verbal noun: one would not say a wall wanted intensely to fall or a tree spoke forcefully.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p73/r8.anchor: ولا تقول: أراد الحائط أن يسقط إرادة شديدة، وقالت الشجرة فمالت، ولا تقول: قالت الشجرة فمالت قولا شديدا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r1.speaker: الفرق الإسلامية
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r1.claim: Islamic theological schools differed: some categorically denied sajʿ in the Quran, while others affirmed it as one of its miraculous aspects.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r1.anchor: اختلفت الفرق الإسلامية بين نفي السجع في القآن نفياً باتاً، والقول بوجوده في النظم القرآني

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r2.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r2.claim: Al-Farra holds that Quranic sajʿ is intended for its own sake and may cause a change of order or word choice to achieve harmony between verse endings.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r2.anchor: مذهب "الفراء" في أن السجع في القرآن مقصود إليه لذاته، وأنه ربما عدل عن نسق إلى آخر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r3.speaker: ابن سنان الخفاجي وابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r3.claim: Ibn Sinan al-Khafaji and Ibn al-Athir deny that Quranic verse-ending meanings are subordinate to their wording.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r3.anchor: وبين من أنكروا، كابن سنان الخفاجي وابن الأثير، أن تكون معاني الفواصل القرآنية تابعة للألفاظ.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r4.speaker: القاضي الباقلاني وعلي بن عيسى الرماني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r4.claim: Al-Baqillani and al-Rummani distinguish Quranic fawasil from sajʿ.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r4.anchor: ورأينا من علماء السلف من فرقوا بين الفواصل والأسجاع، كالقاضي الباقلاني وعلي بن عيسى الرماني.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r5.speaker: أكثر البلاغيين
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r5.claim: Most rhetoricians see no difference between fawasil and sajʿ, and regard the distinction as reluctance to apply a term associated with soothsayers to the Quran.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p267/r5.anchor: وإن لم ير أكثر البلاغيين فرقاً بين الفواصل والسجع، وعندهم أن الأمر في هذه التفرقة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#2/r1.claim: He chose the fleeting worldly life, immersed himself in its pleasures, and made no preparations through faith and obedience for the everlasting afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p36#2/r1.anchor: أي اختار الحياة الدنيا الفانية التي هي على جناح الفوات فانهمك فيما متع به فيها ولم يستعد للحياة الآخرة الأبدية

BINTSHATI:v1p156/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r1.claim: Athar is a lasting sign or trace; to leave an effect is to leave a durable trace, and āthār are remains from earlier people.
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r1.anchor: من علامة باقية. وأثر فيه تأثيراً، ترك فيه أثراً يبقى، والآثار ما بقي من الماضين

BINTSHATI:v1p156/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r2.claim: Īthār means preference, as in Joseph 12:91, al-Aʿlā 87:16, and Ṭā Hā 20:72.
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r2.anchor: والإيثار: التفضيل، وبهذا المعنى جاء في آيات:

BINTSHATI:v1p156/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r3.claim: In al-Ḥashr 59:9, īthār is preferring others over oneself, an expression of generosity and virtue.
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r3.anchor: وجاء نقيضاً للأثرة في آية الحشر 9:

BINTSHATI:v1p156/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r4.claim: Īthār can imply choosing what one judges best and most lasting, while athara can imply keeping the chosen things for oneself.
BINTSHATI:v1p156/r4.anchor: ويجيء الإيثار بمعنى الإختبار، ملحوظاً فيه أن المرء يختار ما يحسبه أفضل وأبقى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r6.claim: Transgression precedes preferring worldly life because it is a major cause of that preference, following natural causal order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r6.anchor: وقدم ذكر الطغيان على إيثار الحياة الدنيا لأن الطغيان من أكبر أسباب إيثار الحياة الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r7.claim: Īthār is preferring one thing over another when one cannot combine the conditions of both.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r7.anchor: والإيثار : تفضيل شيء على شيء في حال لا يتيسر فيها الجمع بين أحوال كل منهما .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r8.claim: The preferred item is a direct object, while what it is preferred over is introduced by ʿalā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r8.anchor: ويعدى فعل الإيثار إلى اسم المأثور بتعدية الفعل إلى مفعوله ، ويعدى إلى المأثور عليه بحرف ( على )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r9.claim: What the item is preferred over may be omitted when the preferred item makes it obvious, as here from the familiar contrast of this life and the Hereafter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r9.anchor: وقد يترك ذكر المأثور عليه إذا كان ذكر المأثور يشير إليه كما إذا كان المأثور والمأثور عليه ضدين كما هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r10.claim: Conversely, the preferred item may be omitted when only what it is preferred over matters; ‘they prefer over themselves’ means the poor, as in al-Ḥashr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r10.anchor: وقد يترك ذكر المأثور اكتفاء بذكر المأثور عليه إذا كان هو الأهم كقوله تعالى : { ويؤثرون على أنفسهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r11.claim: ‘Worldly life’ means its particular benefits and pleasures, not shared with the Hereafter; an implied noun is ‘the bliss of worldly life’.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r11.anchor: والمراد بالحياة الدنيا حظوظها ومنافعها الخاصة بها ، أي التي لا تشاركها فيها حظوظ الآخرة ، فالكلام على حذف مضاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r12.claim: Preferring this life entails rejecting the bliss of the Hereafter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r12.anchor: ويفهم من فعل الإيثار أن معه نبذا لنعيم الآخرة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r13.claim: The preference stems from satisfying the lower self; only divine instruction identifies the interests, including shirk, rejecting messengers, aggression, arrogance, and related vices.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p91/r13.anchor: ويرجع إيثار الحياة الدنيا إلى إرضاء هوى النفس ، وإنما يعرف كلا الحظين بالتوقيف الإلاهي كما عرف الشرك وتكذيب الرسل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#4/r1.claim: He chose worldly life over the afterlife.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#16/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#16/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#16/r1.claim: He prefers worldly life to the Hereafter by following his desires.
